clue.text: An icy blockhouse

parts.note: a blockhouse is normally a timber fort, but here the blocks are of packed snow and ice, an Inuit dwelling

explanation.definitionFit: It is a domed shelter built from blocks of snow, so a house made of icy blocks.

clue.text: Inapt time to become restless

indicators.note: the two words are to become something else, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A badly chosen moment makes someone fidgety and restless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become' turns INAPTTIME into a new nine-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who cannot wait calmly is restless and fidgety.

clue.text: Getting upset, a blockhead can be rough on one

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: a blockhead is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone who gets upset is told that a dimwit may be harsh with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting upset' turns A FOOL round to give the bath sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: This dried gourd is a scrubbing sponge, abrasive on the bather's skin.

clue.text: Musicians roar in a frenzy about the box

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, that is surround, the other piece
letters in a frenzy are thrown about wildly, so the word roar is rearranged

parts.note: a chest is a box

explanation.surface: Players make a noise wildly over the television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the box' looks like television slang, but here it is a container; the frenzied roar splits round it.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large group of instrumental players.

clue.text: An officer of the law studies the company

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
the table can mean the people seated at a meal, the company

explanation.surface: A policeman examines the firm's paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: CON is an old verb for study; 'the table' as diners gathered together is a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is a police officer of the lowest rank.

clue.text: Concern in latter part of life for cash

parts.note: a concern is a business, abbreviated CO for company
age is old age, the last stretch of a lifetime

explanation.surface: Worry in old age about money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concern' reads as worry, but here it is a business, CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Coinage is metal money, the coins in circulation.

clue.text: Unnecessary loss of final point causes annoyance

indicators.note: the last letter is lost from the longer word, the final point dropping off

parts.note: needless means unnecessary
S is south, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Dropping a point late in a game for no reason is irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loss of final' removes the closing S (a compass point) from NEEDLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to irritate or provoke them.

clue.text: Oliver's turn

explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist is Dickens's orphan hero, so his surname; a twist is also a turn or rotation.

clue.text: A garden feature for the far-seeing

definitions.text: A garden feature for the far-seeing

parts.words: A garden feature for the far-seeing
parts.note: a raised summerhouse or turret built in a garden so that visitors can enjoy a distant view

explanation.definitionFit: The Italian name means beautiful view: a gazebo or turret placed for looking out over the scenery.

clue.text: Some regrettably flighty creature

indicators.note: only some of the letters of regrettably are used, a run inside the word

explanation.surface: A bit of a fickle person, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flighty' suggests fickleness, but it means able to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron, a bird that flies.

clue.text: Condemn plagiarism in plain words

indicators.note: the copying is put in the ordinary writing

parts.note: prose is plain writing, not verse
a crib is copied work, plagiarism

explanation.surface: Denounce copying in straightforward language.
explanation.definitionFit: To proscribe is to forbid or denounce something formally.

clue.text: The slacker is one led astray, right?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: led astray means the letters of led wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Is the lazy person someone misled?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes the surface a query about a misled person; the scrambled letters sit between the numeral and the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler is a lazy person who avoids work, a slacker.

clue.text: Bait for badger

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean to torment or pester someone playfully or cruelly.

clue.text: It's not just some old book males and the non-male share

parts.note: not just some but the whole lot is all
OT is the Old Testament, the old book of the Bible
males are men

indicators.note: non- removes the word that follows from the word before it

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: An old text says men and women should divide things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the non-male' is THE with HE taken out, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a portion allocated to someone, their share.

clue.text: Pauline writing

parts.note: not a woman named Pauline's work but a letter by St Paul in the New Testament

explanation.definitionFit: St Paul's New Testament books are letters to churches, such as Romans and Corinthians.

clue.text: Batting badly, get runs and he'll revolt!

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is in

indicators.note: the words get and runs are put together badly, in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A cricketer who bats poorly may rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: IN is cricket for batting; 'badly' shuffles GETRUNS into SURGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent is a rebel who rises against authority.

clue.text: Fashion ads with a point in a depression

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters of ads are reshaped

parts.note: a ness is a headland or promontory, a point of land

explanation.surface: Advertisements for clothing land in a dip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' reorders ADS to SAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Depression here is low spirits, unhappiness.

clue.text: Underworld boss giving a churchman housing and board

indicators.note: the god's name houses, that is contains, the clergyman

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld
a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A gangster offers a cleric lodging and meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld boss' suggests a gangster, but it is Dis, ruler of the dead; 'housing and board' suggests lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: The directors together form a company's board.

clue.text: Rate highly as a flowering plant

parts.note: speed is a rate of movement
well means highly, as in thought well of

explanation.surface: Give high marks to a garden flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell is a small blue-flowered plant of the genus Veronica.

clue.text: Examine a note with a will

parts.note: to test is to examine
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Inspect a letter left with someone's will.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies testate has left a valid will.

clue.text: Peak time before the break

parts.note: the eve is the day or time before an event
a rest is a break

explanation.surface: Busy period ahead of an interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peak time' reads as rush hour, but 'Peak' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the world's highest mountain, in the Himalayas.

clue.text: Get back into the middle and train

indicators.note: the reversed word goes into the word for the centre

parts.note: the core is the middle

indicators.note: get back means the word get is read backwards

explanation.surface: Return to the centre and practise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a verb meaning practise, but it is a noun: a procession.
explanation.definitionFit: A cortege is a funeral procession, a train of mourners.

clue.text: Share top billing with daughter in "Love's Labour's Lost' '

parts.note: to costar is to share top billing in a film or play

explanation.surface: A star and their daughter both head the bill in a Shakespeare comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a character in the play: COSTARD is the clown in Love's Labour's Lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Costard is the rustic clown in that Shakespeare comedy.

clue.text: Catch the French entering the-craft without anything to hang onto!

indicators.note: the catch and the French article go into the vessel's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a craft
a trap is a catch
les is French for the

explanation.surface: French passengers get caught boarding a boat with nothing to hold.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'the-craft' is a printing slip; the craft is a steamship, and the exclamation hints at a wardrobe mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: A strapless dress or top has no shoulder straps holding it up.

clue.text: Sabbath drive to see the river

parts.note: S abbreviates Sabbath, as in the calendar
a tour is a drive or trip

explanation.surface: A Sunday outing to look at the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stour is the name of several English rivers.

clue.text: Writer on the church makes little money

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An author who writes about religion earns little.
explanation.definitionFit: Pence are the smallest British coins, small amounts of cash.

clue.text: Criticised about money issue

indicators.note: the word for criticised goes about, around, the money

parts.note: chid is an old past tense of chide, criticise
L is the pound sign, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Attacked over a financial problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' suggests a problem, but here it means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a legal word for offspring.

clue.text: Grabbing an animal that's to be put out

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is grabs, holding inside, the creature

parts.note: i.e. is short for id est, that is
a rat is an animal

explanation.surface: Seizing a creature that is about to be released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' looks like let outside, but it means annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone put out is annoyed, angry.

clue.text: The main canoe-user

indicators.note: the word canoe is used, its letters put to use in another order

explanation.surface: The chief paddler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is a poetic word for the sea; a canoe user would be found on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is the open sea in old poetic usage.

clue.text: Package being returned, give an address with added detail

indicators.note: the package word is returned, read backwards

parts.note: a bale is a bundled package
to orate is to make a speech

explanation.surface: A parcel coming back, write a delivery address with more information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give an address' suggests a postal label, but it means make a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate means intricate, worked out in detail.

clue.text: Repeatedly played the host when retired

parts.note: re means again, doing it once more
a host treats guests

explanation.surface: Hosted again and again on leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean withdrew or went back.

clue.text: Inflation is fine for the Americans

explanation.definitionFit: A swell is a swelling or expansion; swell is also American slang for excellent.
